bets.summary: Deep pass REVERSES the first pass on SMU team total Over 30.5 and on Over 51.5. The new key factor is weather: FOX 4 DFW's Oct. 17 forecast has showers and storms building from late morning, with stronger cells (gusts of 55-60 mph, quarter-size hail) most likely 1-4 p.m. CT. That window overlaps an 11 a.m. CT kickoff and raises the chance of a lightning delay. Both offenses are also in a slump. SMU had 218 total yards and Jennings 160 passing against BC before the bye. Virginia scored 7 at Florida State and 21 against West Virginia, then managed 288 yards against Syracuse (Pribula 11-19 for 119). The total has already fallen from 52.5 at open to 51.5. SMU's ML remains the most likely winner: home, off a bye, 3-0 at Ford, a defense with 5 sacks and 14 TFL in its last game, and a UVA secondary missing CB Agard (out for the season) with safeties Costner and Hillman doubtful. The Under is the best edge.

legs.note: Best edge. The forecast has storms near kickoff with strong wind and hail risk, which could bring a delay, a slick ball and more running. SMU's offense is slumping (218 yards against BC, 160 passing). Virginia's offense is run-first (Middlebrook) with a QB who has gone 11-19 for 119 yards and scored 7 against FSU. The total has moved down from 52.5 to 51.5. SP+ projects about 53 points, which is the main argument for the over.

legs.note: Martinez allows about 7 hits per 9 innings (1.09 WHIP), and the market expects about 12 outs from him. That projects around 3 hits, so he needs a bad night to allow 4.
legs.status: Confirmed starter; took a liner off the back in the ALDS clincher, no injury since

bets.summary: Deep pass keeps the first pass's direction but changes the reasoning and the ranking. Oregon (3-2) is -7 / 51.5 at home. QB Dante Moore (concussion) is OUT, and CBS (Zenitz/Hummer) reports that third-stringer Brock Thomas, a former preferred walk-on with 20 career-relevant attempts in 2026 (14/20, 172 yds, 1 TD), makes his first start over Dylan Raiola. Top WR Evan Stewart (27-352-4) was downgraded to DOUBTFUL on the Big Ten availability report, and WR Jeremiah McClellan is also out. Nebraska (5-1) brings an Aurich 4-2-5 defense allowing 15.2 ppg and 276 ypg, and it held No. 7 Indiana to 328 yds and 65 rush yds. Caveat: the schedule was soft before Indiana. ESPN FPI has the teams only 2.1 points apart (Oregon 19.5, Nebraska 17.4). STRONGEST EDGE: Oregon team total Under 29.5. MOST LIKELY TO WIN: Oregon ML (fair 0.69). I rate it about 0.66 because of the QB downgrade, so it carries negative edge. Nebraska +7 is a modest lean, with Rhule's road and ranked-opponent record and pro money on Oregon pulling against it. No player props.

legs.note: The FPI gap of 2.1 plus home field projects Oregon by about 5 with Moore. With Thomas starting, 7 looks generous, and a low-scoring game makes the number more valuable. Against it: Colandrea took 5 sacks vs Indiana (25/43, 255) and now faces Oregon's DL (Uiagalelei, Tuioti, Washington), Rhule's road and ranked-opponent record is poor, and the line held at -7/-7.5 despite heavy public tickets on Nebraska.

bets.summary: Deep pass confirms the first pass's core read and does not reverse it. ESPN's Pete Thamel and the Friday SEC availability report have MSST QB Kamario Taylor (turf toe; 69.2% completions, 14 TD / 2 INT, a Heisman-list QB) doubtful and not expected to play, and RB Fluff Bothwell (403 yds, team leader) doubtful too. MSST would go to walk-on redshirt freshman Parker 'Billy' Puckett (8-for-14, 89 yds in 2026) and/or veteran transfer AJ Swann (Vanderbilt/App State, about 57% career completions, 32 TD / 17 INT). The spread moved from about -10 to -17.5 and the total from 58.5-59.5 to 56. The new finding is that Swann is a real veteran fallback, which caps how far the MSST offense falls. The MSST team total Under 19.5 is still the strongest edge. LSU ML is now added as the leg most likely to win, and the full-game Under is downgraded slightly because both teams have gone over the total often (LSU 4/6, MSST 3/5).

legs.desc: Mississippi State Bulldogs team total Under 19.5
legs.note: Strongest edge. MSST loses its QB and lead RB against an LSU front allowing 47.5 rush ypg and recording nearly 4 sacks a game (MSST allowed 5 sacks vs Alabama). Puckett was a preferred walk-on, and Swann has a career 56-59% completion rate with a high INT rate (8 INTs in 7 games at App State in 2025). Counterpoints are that MSST scored 23 or more in all five games and that LSU's defense is missing LB Whit Weeks (broken leg), S Dashawn Spears, and possibly LB Tylen Singleton, which leaves room for garbage-time points.

bets.summary: Deep pass keeps the first pass's Indiana lean, but moves the top leg to Indiana +3.5 (-124, fair 0.528), the leg most likely to win, and adds the Indiana ML as a value angle. The models cluster near a pick'em: SP+ has OSU 26-25 (+0.9, 52%), ESPN FPI has OSU by under a point (one SI piece has IND at 50.6%), and Scores&Stats has IND by 7.1. Kalshi prices IND +3.5 at 53%. Every named analyst found (Covers, Action Network, Yahoo, BUSR/GoldSheet, Predictem, TheSpread) is on Indiana ATS. OSU (5-1; its loss was 24-23 to Texas after leading 20-3) is missing starting OT Austin Siereveld (out) and RB Ja'Kobi Jackson (out), and third-string RB Isaiah West is questionable. Hoover has 17 TD and 0 INT. The total stays a coin flip, and the edge for the Under and the OSU team-total Under is small. Indiana +3 at -110 (fair 0.503) is the best-priced spread edge.

legs.desc: Ohio State Buckeyes team total Under 26.5
legs.note: Price +100 at BetMGM, fair 0.482. SP+ projects OSU at 26 and GoldSheet at 20, and Action's projected range is 20-27 for the winner. OSU had 10 points and 58 rush yds on 26 carries against this defense last Dec. It is now without OT Siereveld and RB depth (Ja'Kobi Jackson out; West questionable; freshman Legend Bey would be RB2). On the other side, OSU has scored 42+ in its recent games (45-16 over Maryland) and Smith leads the FBS in receiving.

bets.summary: Deep pass mostly confirms the first pass and adds a Texas team-total under. Florida (4-2, losses of 45-17 at Missouri and to South Carolina, where it conceded 38) is expected to start sophomore Tramell Jones Jr., who has a small career sample: 44/64, 443 yds, 4 TD, 2 INT across 2025-26. Aaron Philo (shoulder) is still questionable, and no official starter was confirmed as of 12:45Z. Texas (4-1) allows about 16 ppg but scores only about 31 ppg, with a stop-start offense (20-17 at Tennessee, 30-6 vs UTSA, 24-27 vs Oklahoma) and Manning sacked 8 times in two games. So this deep pass leans toward a low-scoring game rather than a blowout. The most likely leg to win is Texas ML. The strongest edge is Florida team total Under 19.5. Florida +11 is dropped: the first pass's ATS and history lean does not outweigh the backup-QB downgrade.

legs.note: This is the strongest edge. Without Philo, Florida's offense runs through Baugh against a run defense allowing about 96 rush yards/game. Jones's sample is 5.5 YPA in 2025 and 2 INT on 29 attempts in 2026. Florida scored 17 at Missouri, its only true road test against a quality defense. The fair price is 0.49, and a 20+ point outcome needs a short field or turnovers.

bets.summary: Deep pass on No. 7 Alabama (5-1) at No. 15 Tennessee (5-1), 3:30 ET ABC at Neyland. This pass partly reverses the first one. The first pass leaned on Alabama's pass defense being 103rd in yards, but SI's opponent-adjusted numbers put Alabama's defense 7th in adjusted EPA/play and Alabama's offense 4th in success rate. Tennessee's pass offense is 121st in EPA/pass and 126th in pass success rate, and it now starts sophomore George MacIntyre (one career start: 18/29, 247 yds, 1 TD, 2 INT at Arkansas) with Faizon Brandon questionable with a shoulder injury. Models cluster around Alabama by about 7 (Dimers 30-23, 73.8%; FPI 69.8%; Rocky Top Insider 29-22), so +7.5/+8 is close to fair and no longer a real lean. The best edge is Tennessee's offense, and Alabama ML is the leg most likely to win. Risks on Alabama's side: freshman QB Keelon Russell has 3 turnovers on the road at Kentucky and went 16/30 against Georgia, WR Ryan Coleman-Williams is out, C Racin Delgatty is doubtful, Tennessee's pass rush got 6 sacks on Texas, and Tennessee has won the last two meetings at Neyland.

legs.note: Two elite-by-adjusted-numbers defenses meet a backup QB and a freshman QB, and Alabama is missing its top WR and maybe its center. Sharp money took the total from 55 (Circa open) to 51 (SBG: 'sharps like the under'; WagerTalk Under 51.5). Models are close to the number (Dimers 53, RTI 51, CBS model leans Over), so most of the value is already gone.

bets.summary: Deep pass keeps the first-pass direction (Missouri side, game under) but tightens it. Changes: (1) the side moves from Missouri +5 to Missouri +5.5, the half point better at a slightly higher fair price, because SP+ rates this close to a pick'em (Predictem: Ole Miss favored by under 0.5 at home), while the market says 5.5; (2) 1H Under 35.5 is added as the leg most likely to win. The 1H main line is 30.5, and the forecast (NWS: sunny, 65F, NNE wind about 15 mph, gusts near 20) plus Missouri's run-heavy, clock-draining plan make a 36+ point first half unlikely; (3) corrected record context: Missouri's one loss was 31-24 at Mississippi State (Sep 26), its 8th straight loss to a ranked SEC team, and that tempers the Missouri case. Ole Miss's one loss was 52-28 at Florida, where Florida ran for 302 yards. Both QBs are healthy (Simmons is off the report) and Missouri RB Ahmad Hardy is out. Missouri's havoc defense (4th nationally, 3 sacks per game) meets an Ole Miss OL that allows about 1 sack per game and an offense that has scored on 20 of 20 red-zone trips, so the edges are modest. No player props (Ohio).

legs.note: SportsLine's 10,000-simulation model projects 57 points (Under about 53%). SBR, TheRx and Covers take the under, while Bleacher Nation and LVSB take the over. Missouri is 4-1 to the under in its last 5, and the under is 8-2 in Ole Miss's last 10 games as a home favorite. Wind and Missouri's possession-length plan help the under. Against it, the teams average 38.8 and 35.8 ppg, and Ole Miss's defense ranks 123rd on third down.

bets.summary: Deep pass: No. 2 Notre Dame (6-0, 16 straight wins, all by double digits) at No. 8 BYU (5-0 SU/ATS), 5:30 PM MT, GameDay crowd. The core view stays the same, but the ranking changes: Notre Dame ML is now the anchor and most-likely-to-win leg, the BYU team-total under is the best edge, and ND -10.5 drops to a thin lean because experts are split (Covers/SI/Predictem/AtoZ on ND; VegasInsider/ATS.io on BYU) and Freeman is only 2-4 in true road games. BYU's offense without RB LJ Martin (out 4-6 wks) scored 24 vs Iowa State and 17 at TCU, and now faces the FBS No. 1 total defense (214 ypg, 11.0 ppg). Correction to the first pass: the 2022 meeting was ND 28-20, not 20-16.

legs.note: ND's 16-game double-digit streak and the Martin injury support the cover, as do Covers (Powers, ND by 13), SI, Predictem and AtoZ (30-15). Against it: BYU is 5-0 ATS, VegasInsider and ATS.io take BYU +10.5, public tickets are on BYU, and ND's road résumé under Freeman is weak. This is close to a coin flip, so keep it a lean.

bets.summary: This deeper pass sharpens the first pass's Under/Wisconsin lean but does not reverse it. The headline Under is now UCLA team total Under 23.5, which is also the leg most likely to win. With Iamaleava, UCLA's offense was already weaker than its 39.2 ppg suggests: at Oregon it rushed for only 79 yards and needed a +4 turnover margin (Oregon gave it away 7 times) to win 17-15. Now Ty Dieffenbach makes his first start. In 2025 at Cal Poly (FCS) he went 56.8% for 1,305 yds, 9 TD and 9 INT, and he never played at Pitt. He faces a rested Wisconsin defense that allows 3.2 yds per rush and leads the league in pass defense. On the other side, Colton Joseph (56.6%, 7.9 YPA, 10 TD, 5 INT; 3 INTs at PSU) is turnover-prone against UCLA's ball-hawking defense, so Wisconsin's scoring is also limited. The market agrees: the total has fallen from 44.5 (49.5 at one book) to 42.5-43, and Action Network splits show Wisconsin with about 23% of bets but 77% of the money, with the spread moving from 3 to 2.5. Wisconsin +2.5 is the sharp-side lean, but SI and the Sports Gambling Podcast trio still lay the points with UCLA, so the side is closer to a coin flip than the totals are.

legs.note: STRONGEST EDGE versus fair (about 50%), because you get the best of the number after the total fell from 44.5-49.5. Both offenses are run-first and clock-killing (UCLA held the ball 39:15 at Oregon). UCLA's last game went 32 total points, and Wisconsin's games against PSU and MSU went 44 and 34. The Under is 7-3 in Wisconsin's last 10. The risk is turnover-driven scoring: Joseph has 5 INTs, and UCLA backup S Ta'Shawn James already has 3 INTs.

bets.summary: The deeper pass finds the Oklahoma offense is in worse shape than the first pass showed. It ranks 127th in offensive success rate (37%) and 132nd in EPA per rush, and Mateer has 6 turnover-worthy throws in 60 SEC attempts. Friday's report also listed a third offensive-line starter as doubtful (RG Heath Ozaeta, who played 59 snaps vs Texas), alongside LT Fasusi and G Pierre-Louis, with true freshman Noah Best and Peyton Joseph expected to fill in. That strengthens the Oklahoma team total under 24.5, the best edge. I've reversed the first pass's side lean from OU -6.5 to Kentucky +6.5: Kentucky ranks 17th in offensive success rate and protects the ball, OU starting CB Eli Bowen is out, Venables teams have a weak record after big wins, and most projections put the margin at 6 or less. Oklahoma ML (about 68%) is the leg most likely to win. Ozaeta's downgrade is the only new availability news. Kentucky's DB/LB absences were already known.

legs.note: This reverses the first pass. Oklahoma's offense can't stretch a lead: it ranks 127th in success rate and 132nd in EPA/rush, and three OL starters are doubtful. Its four FBS games produced 10, 14, 13 and 27 points, and the 27 against Texas included defensive and special-teams touchdowns. Most projections put the margin at 6 or 7 or less: Dimers and DRatings 7, TeamRankings 6, Grueling Truth 3, Predictem 6, Yahoo 6, and JD PicKell has Kentucky winning. Andy Staples and Ari Wasserman both take Kentucky. The case against: 79-84% of tickets are on Kentucky, so this is the public side, and +6.5 sits just under the key number of 7.
